root_idea.summary: The root gathers three principal semantic orientations: greatness and magnitude, encompassing or covering, and sound with associated movement.
root_idea.development: The first orientation extends from physical thickness or largeness to greatness, dignity, and divine majesty. A second denotes taking the bulk of something or covering it throughout. A third concerns ringing or reverberating sound and related movement or agitation.

senses.definition: Supreme greatness or majesty, especially the divine majesty of God.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran, it occurs in the expression ذُو الجَلَالِ وَالإِكْرَامِ, describing God as possessing majesty and honor; the greatness denoted is absolute and beyond full comprehension.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Thick, gross, coarse, rough, large, bulky, or great in physical size.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of material substances and large-bodied things, including a large-bodied camel; opposed to دَقِيق or دِقّ in the sense of fine, small, or slender.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Greatness in estimation, rank, or dignity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A general Classical sense of greatness or high standing, distinct from the Quranic use of absolute divine majesty.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Great or eminent in rank; a person or group of distinction, nobility, or high standing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to persons and groups, including chiefs or people of rank.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An exclamatory intensifier meaning “how greatly” or “how very much.”
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in an emphatic exclamatory construction such as جَلَّ مَا بَعُدَتْ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become old or advanced in age, and firm or sound in judgment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to people, camels, and other specified living subjects.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be too young to bear offspring.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A contrary lexical use in the expression جَلَّتِ الهَاجِنُ عَنِ الوَلَدِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go forth or emigrate from one country, town, or dwelling to another; a departing or exiled group.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The derived noun جَالٌّ may denote one who departs, and جَالَّةٌ a departing or exiled population.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The greater, main, principal, or chief part of something; its bulk or mass.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The associated verb may mean to take the greater part or main portion of something.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bring an injury or harmful consequence upon oneself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic construction such as جَلَلْتَ هَذَا عَلَى نَفْسِكَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pick up or collect animal dung, sometimes specifically for use as fuel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object is camel, sheep, goat, or similar dung.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To include, cover, or envelop something throughout its general extent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of rain or clouds covering the land, including it within the extent of their fall; the construction may also simply mean to cover a thing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ascend, rise, mount, or get upon or over something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived Form II use describing movement onto or over an object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To clothe or equip a horse or other beast with a protective covering.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The related passive participle denotes an animal clad with such a covering.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make thick, gross, large, or great.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative use opposed to making something fine or small.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To magnify, honor, or exalt someone in rank or station.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of honoring God or a person and recognizing greatness or majesty.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To give much or a large amount.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May describe giving a large feed, such as a substantial quantity of grain to a horse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To give someone a mature she-camel, or conversely not to give either a mature camel or a young camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized livestock-giving construction contrasting a mature animal with a young or small one.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become strong; in another reported use, to become weak.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The two contrary meanings are attributed to the same derived form in different usage traditions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To sit upon or mount an animal, including mounting it sexually.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of sitting upon a horse and of a stallion mounting a she-camel; the construction is not restricted to the gender or class of the object beyond the cited animal usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To exalt oneself above something, hold oneself aloof from it, or disdain it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Constructed with عَنْ or عَلَى and describing self-elevation or disdain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To sound, ring, or produce a vehement reverberating sound; by extension, to threaten.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a little bell, thunder, or other loud sound; a related construction can denote a threatening utterance from behind a covering or concealment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a horse, to neigh clearly or distinctly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized animal-sound use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To move or shake something by hand; to shuffle, mix, or twist it vigorously.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of moving gaming arrows, mixing an object, or strongly twisting a bowstring or similar cord.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become in motion, or to be put into motion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive or passive-like motion use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become agitated or disturbed in the mind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative internal-state use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To sink, become depressed, or subside.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of foundations or other structures that sink or give way.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The sail of a ship.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal nautical use, with a plural form also reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small, easy, mean, paltry, or contemptible matter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A contrary value of جَلَلٌ or related forms, opposite to the sense of something great or momentous.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A covering, especially a protective horse-cloth; also a cover for a book or volume.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The covering may protect a horse or similar beast from cold, or cover written material.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The place where a tent or house is pitched and constructed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal sense for a building or encampment site.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The rose, including its white, red, and yellow varieties; also jasmine.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plant name identified as an Arabicized Persian loanword.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The stalks of grain or other seed-produce after reaping, including stalks left in the field.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may distinguish the reaped stalks from تِبْن after threshing and cutting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Animal dung, especially that of camels, sheep, goats, or similar animals; by metonymy, human ordure.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May denote a single lump or unbroken piece and, in later use, dung mixed with chopped straw and dried as fuel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A large woven palm-leaf receptacle, especially a basket or container for dates.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may also serve other practical container or covering purposes.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The portion taken from cattle; in the associated verbal construction, to take or consume that portion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical branch reported in connection with taking the edible or usable part of cattle, distinct from the general sense of greatness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A great, momentous, formidable, hard, difficult, severe, or distressing matter or event.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of an affair, case, or event of substantial consequence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: On account of, for the sake of, or because of someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in the idiomatic prepositional construction مِنْ جَلَلِكَ and its variants.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A particle equivalent to نَعَمْ, meaning “yes.”
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A grammatical particle use attributed to a Classical authority.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The deck or roof-like part of a ship.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A singular nautical noun, also connected in the lexicon with coverings or ship sails.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A large palm tree bearing abundant fruit.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized botanical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A species of ثُمَام, a weak panic-grass or panicum used to stop the interstices of houses.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plant noun with a reported plural جَلَائِلُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A large-bodied or substantial she-camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is distinct from the homonymous term for an animal that eats filth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A seller of protective coverings for horses or similar beasts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A relational noun derived from جُلّ, the animal covering.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An animal that repeatedly eats filth or human ordure, especially a cow; by extension, the animal's milk or flesh is prohibited.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized legal and livestock term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small bell, especially a hollow metal bell hung on a horse, similar beast, or hawk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The associated plural is جَلَاجِلُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To imperil or endanger oneself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use of hanging or tying a little bell, denoting bold exposure to danger or notoriety.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The fruit of coriander or sesame, including sesame in its husk before reaping and its grain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical and agricultural noun with more than one reported application.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The core or kernel of the heart.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative expression for the innermost center of a person's feelings or thoughts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: That which is great in estimation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal use distinct from the botanical term جُلْجُلَان.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An ass that brays clearly; also a she-camel with a similarly clear call.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An animal epithet derived from clear or resonant sound.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A boy who is lively, brisk, sprightly, or light in spirit.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An epithet for energetic conduct and work.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To reveal what is agitated or stirred in one's mind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in the construction أَبْثَثْتُهُ جُلَاجِلَ نَفْسِي.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The poll-tax, derived from the term for a departing or expelled population.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantivized administrative and fiscal use; the related feminine or collective form may denote its payer population.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Greater, greatest, thicker, or thickest; by extension, most exalted or majestic.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: With the definite article it may be applied to God as a superlative epithet.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The act of magnifying or honoring.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal noun comparable to تَكْرِمَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A written page, book, volume, or other writing containing knowledge; hence, a journal or periodical.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may denote any book or written work, including a work of poetry.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Knowledge or a body of doctrine, especially practical legal science.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A semantic extension from a written repository of knowledge.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Water into which animal or human dung has fallen.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized descriptive term derived from جَلَّة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person exceptionally excellent or elegant in mind, manners, speech, appearance, or conduct, with no evident fault.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An evaluative epithet for a faultless or highly accomplished person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A camel that has attained full strength.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized livestock epithet.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Camels bearing small bells.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the plural expression إِبِلٌ مُجَلْجَلَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cloud containing or producing the sound of thunder; by extension, sounding rain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Distinct from مُجَلِّل, which describes rain covering the land rather than thunderous sound.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A strong or formidable chief, or a bold, forceful, eloquent person whose voice or fame reaches far.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The epithet can include courage in exposing oneself to peril and vigor in defending or repelling.

cautions: The Quranic form is the noun جَلَال in the expression ذُو الجَلَالِ وَالإِكْرَامِ; the broader physical, social, idiomatic, and derived-form meanings belong to Classical Arabic usage rather than to this Quranic occurrence.
Lane's entry is matched through the contracted geminate root جَل; its source units have therefore been retained in the internal coverage ledger without treating every derived form as a Quranic form.
